fact.text: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood: two hearts pump blood through the gills, and the third pumps it around the rest of the body.

heads_up: Nuo lapkričio 20 d. įsigalioja nauja telefonų pardavimo išsimokėtinai tvarka.
Savaitgalį atšals, keliuose galimas plikledis ir pirmasis sniegas.

lithuania.headline: Referendumas dėl šeimos sampratos kovą nevyks
lithuania.summary: Teisės ir teisėtvarkos komitetui pusmetį nepateikus išvados, patariamasis referendumas nebegali vykti kartu su 2027 m. kovo 7 d. savivaldos rinkimais, nes jį reikėjo paskelbti iki gruodžio 7 d. Iniciatoriai kaltina komiteto pirmininką Julių Sabatauską sabotažu ir sieks referendumo per 2028 m. Seimo rinkimus.
lithuania.context: Po 2024 m. Seimo rinkimų valdančiojoje koalicijoje esantys valstiečiai kartu su kitais dešiniaisiais pavasarį inicijavo patariamąjį referendumą, ar Konstitucijoje įrašyti, kad šeima kyla tik iš vyro ir moters santuokos, motinystės ir tėvystės. Tai atsakas į Konstitucinio Teismo sprendimus, pripažinusius ir kitų porų teises. Balandį projektas įveikė pateikimą, bet įstrigo komitete, o valstiečiai ir LLRA-KŠS grasina dėl to nebalsuoti už kitų metų biudžetą.

lithuania.headline: Lietuva kitąmet nepriims migrantų pagal ES planą – mokės
lithuania.summary: Seimo komitetai pritarė ministro Martyno Katelyno siūlymui kitąmet nepriimti nė vieno migranto pagal ES solidarumo mechanizmą, o sumokėti įnašą, kurio dydis dar neaiškus; galutinį sprendimą priims Vyriausybė. Šiemet Lietuva sutiko priimti 58 migrantus iš Kipro ir sumokėti 1,4 mln. eurų.
lithuania.context: ES solidarumo mechanizmas įpareigoja šalis padėti valstybėms, į kurias migrantai atvyksta pirmiausia: priimti dalį jų arba mokėti. Ministras atmeta kaltinimus ksenofobija ir sako, kad mokėti per penkerius metus bus pigiau.

lithuania.headline: Pagalbinis apvaisinimas taps prieinamas ir vienišoms moterims
lithuania.summary: Prezidentas Gitanas Nausėda pasirašė pataisas, pagal kurias pagalbiniu apvaisinimu galės naudotis ne tik sutuoktiniai ir registruoti partneriai, bet ir neregistruotos poros bei vienišos moterys. Valstybė apmokės gydymą diagnozavus nevaisingumą, o vaisingoms vienišoms moterims teks mokėti pačioms.
lithuania.context: Pataisų imtasi po 2025 m. balandžio Konstitucinio Teismo nutarimo, kad šias paslaugas riboti tik sutuoktiniams ir registruotiems partneriams prieštarauja Konstitucijai.

world.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen
world.summary: After separate talks with Xi Jinping and a 40-minute meeting with Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump joins the first-ever three-way summit of the US, Chinese and Russian leaders at APEC in Shenzhen, expected to cover Ukraine, Iran, nuclear arms and AI. Trump said the US and China want to help end the war in Ukraine, while Xi called US-China relations stable and improved.
world.why: Top story across BBC, Google News and Lithuanian outlets
world.context: The three powers have rarely been further apart: Russia has been at war with Ukraine since its full-scale invasion in February 2022, China has backed Moscow economically, and the US and China have spent years in trade and tech disputes. Trump returned to the White House in January 2025 promising to end the Ukraine war quickly, but peace talks have repeatedly stalled.

world.headline: Anthropic raises $81bn in the biggest IPO ever
world.summary: The Claude maker sold 980 million shares at $83, above its $70–78 range, raising $81.3bn and valuing it at about $1.5tn; it starts trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT. That beats SpaceX's $75bn debut in June and makes Anthropic the first purely AI company to list in the US.
world.why: Covered by 6 outlets, BBC front page
world.context: Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers.

world.headline: Israeli tanks cross Gaza's 'yellow line'
world.summary: Israeli forces made their first ground incursion into Hamas-controlled central Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire, advancing near Nuseirat camp to destroy what they called a terror tunnel and forcing displaced families to flee. Hamas called it a flagrant ceasefire violation; medics reported at least one person killed in a nearby airstrike.
world.context: The war began on 7 October 2023, when Hamas attacked Israel, killing about 1,200 people, and Israel responded with a devastating offensive on Gaza. A US-brokered ceasefire in October 2025 left Israel holding more than 60% of the strip behind the so-called yellow line, but near-daily strikes have continued and both sides accuse each other of violations.

world.headline: Muslims set to outnumber Christians by 2035
world.summary: A Pew Research Center study of 201 countries projects that Islam will overtake Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, mainly because Muslims are younger and have more children. Pakistan is expected to pass Indonesia as the country with the most Muslims, while India stays more than three-quarters Hindu.

interesting.headline: GTA 6 launches with a record-tying 99 score
interesting.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is out on PS5 and Xbox after a 13-year wait, with critics calling it a masterpiece and a Metacritic average of 99, tying Ocarina of Time's record. Pre-orders topped 15.8 million copies and $1.5bn, and it broke the all-time livestream viewer record before release.
interesting.context: It is the first new GTA since GTA V in 2013 and reportedly cost over $1bn to make.

interesting.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon
interesting.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a model it says matches its top Carbon tier's quality at the speed of its fast Flash models; it is live for AI Pro subscribers.

interesting.headline: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m
interesting.summary: Sotheby's sold Chestnut Trees in Blossom, painted in the last two months of Van Gogh's life, for $190.4m, smashing his previous auction record of $117.2m. A last-minute deal settled claims by a German family's heirs that it had been sold under Nazi-era duress.

interesting.headline: Pierce Brosnan backs Robert Pattinson as Bond
interesting.summary: Former 007 Pierce Brosnan publicly welcomed Robert Pattinson, who was announced on Monday as the new James Bond, telling him he will be magnificent.
interesting.why: Covered by Variety and The Hollywood Reporter

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: The Crimean bridge was hit for a third time this week early on Thursday, halting traffic and trains, just before Putin's summit with Trump and Xi. The EU proposed a €45bn loan to Kyiv, to be repaid only after Russia pays reparations.
ongoing.context: Russia seized Crimea in 2014 and launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. After Kyiv pushed Russian troops back from the capital and parts of the south that year, the front largely froze into a war of attrition fought with drones and missiles. Kyiv has long targeted the Kerch bridge, Russia's main link to Crimea, and this week brought down a section of its road.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Trump is weighing new strikes on Iran as Israel warns of chemical weapons, while Gulf states try to head off an all-out war; the US and Iran traded more strikes, including one on a UAE oil tanker.
ongoing.context: Tensions go back to the 1979 revolution, and rose again after the US left the nuclear deal in 2018. Israel and the US struck Iran's nuclear sites in June 2025, and this autumn the confrontation turned into open US-Iran fighting around the Gulf. This week a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island was followed by Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain.

ongoing.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
ongoing.update: Nvidia delayed its quarterly SEC report, telling analysts it may need to add risk disclosures about the Huang investigation; Trump said he raised Huang's case briefly with Xi.
ongoing.context: Earlier this month Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang admitted an affair with an executive of Megaspeed, a firm suspected of selling restricted Nvidia chips to China, who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. He stepped down last week, and Nvidia's board has ruled out bringing him back. Congress, the Justice Department and reportedly the SEC are investigating.

ongoing.title: Saudi Arabia-Houthi fighting
ongoing.update: A Houthi missile threat towards Riyadh caused damage, the Saudi-led coalition said.
ongoing.context: Yemen's Houthi rebels seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, and a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 to restore the government. A truce from 2022 largely held for years, but fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia has flared up again in recent weeks.
